### CD59-like glycoprotein `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PR_000001809`
#### Removed
- [CD59-like glycoprotein](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PR_000001809) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "Category=gene. Requested by=CL. Pro-orthology refers to, in this case, after-speciation gene duplication in the non-human species (aka 1:many orthology). This gene is present as a single copy in human and has undergone a lineage-specific duplication in mouse. CD59 antigen has a core architecture consisting of one UPAR/Ly-6 domain (Pfam:PF00021), a small domain of about 70 amino acids and containing 5 conserved disulfide bonds. It is both N- and O-glycosylated and is a GPI-anchored protein that releases soluble forms in some tissues." 

#### Added
- [CD59-like glycoprotein](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PR_000001809) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "Category=gene. Requested by=CL. Note: Pro-orthology refers to, in this case, after-speciation gene duplication in the non-human species (aka 1:many orthology). This gene is present as a single copy in human and has undergone a lineage-specific duplication in mouse. CD59 antigen has a core architecture consisting of one UPAR/Ly-6 domain (Pfam:PF00021), a small domain of about 70 amino acids and containing 5 conserved disulfide bonds. It is both N- and O-glycosylated and is a GPI-anchored protein that releases soluble forms in some tissues."

### Cerebral edema `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0002181`

#### Added
- Class: [Cerebral edema](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0002181) 

- [Cerebral edema](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0002181) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "Cerebral edema refers to swelling within brain tissue due to the accumulation of fluid, and can occur as in response to almost any insulting agent. Edema canbe observed in and around regions of dead or dying brain, around metastases and abscesses, after traumatic injury, following hypoxic ischemic injury, and around primary brain tumors. There are at least five different types of edema: vasogenic, cytotoxic, hydrostatic, interstitial, and hypoosmotic. Three effects of edema are visible on imaging: (i) loss of gray-white matter differentiation; (ii) swelling of sulci (shrinking of gyri); and (iii) mass effects. On CT scanning, extensive low density may represent vasogenic edema. As the brain swells, not only do the sulci decrease, but all of the CSF spaces of the hemispheres (including the ventricles) decrease as well. Magnetic resonance tomography may show abnormalities of diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), and Fluid attenuation inversion recovery (FLAIR) sequences. Phenotype terms involving cerebral edema thus reflect inference about the underlying processes responsible for these abnormalities on brain imaging." 

- [Cerebral edema](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0002181) [label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "Cerebral edema" 

- [Cerebral edema](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0002181) EquivalentTo [has part](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_0000051) some 
([edematous](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001450) and ([characteristic of part of](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0002314) some [telencephalon](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_0001893)) and ([has modifier](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0002573) some [abnormal](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000460)))

### Coarctation of aorta `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0001680`

#### Added
- Class: [Coarctation of aorta](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0001680) 

- [Coarctation of aorta](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0001680) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "Coarctation refers to a narrowing of the lumen of a vessel producing an obstruction to flow. Coarctation can occur in any region of the aorta. Coarctation of the aorta is often a discrete obstruction commonly located in the descending thoracic aorta. More specifically, it is usually located in the juxtaductal position immediately distal to the left-subclavian artery in a left-sided arch. The hallmark clinical finding in coarctation of the aorta is hypertension proximal to the lesion, with diminished blood pressure distal to the obstruction. Consequently, clinical diagnosis can be made by the presence of diminished lower extremity pulses, differences in timing between upper extremity central pulses (often brachial) and lower extremity central pulses (often femoral), or the presence of a supine arm-leg blood pressure gradient." 

- [Coarctation of aorta](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0001680) [label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "Coarctation of aorta" 

- [Coarctation of aorta](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0001680) EquivalentTo [has part](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_0000051) some 
([constricted](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001847) and ([characteristic of](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0000052) some [aorta](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_0000947)) and ([has modifier](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0002573) some [abnormal](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000460))) 

- [Coarctation of aorta](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0001680) SubClassOf [Abnormal aortic morphology](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0001679) 

- [Coarctation of aorta](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0001680) SubClassOf [has part](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_0000051) some

### Pulmonic stenosis `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0001642`

- [Pulmonic stenosis](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0001642) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "Pulmonic stenosis is often seen as a part of Fallot' s tetralogy, in which case the events leading to the formation of the overriding aorta are also believed to be a cause of the pulmonic stenosis. The degree of stenosis varies between individuals with TOF, and is the primary determinant of symptoms and severity."

- [Tricuspid stenosis](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_0010446) [comment](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment) "Tricuspid stenosis results in characteristic changes in the jugular venous pulse in the form of leisurely V to Y descent and prominent a-waves. The liver is enlarged with a firm edge and is pulsatile in presystole. This is best appreciated with one hand on the liver edge and one on the precordium. Auscultation reveals a low- to medium-pitched diastolic rumble with inspiratory accentuation. This is usually localized to the lower sternal border."

### class prediction objective `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200179`
#### Removed
- Class: [class prediction objective](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200179) 

- [class prediction objective](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200179) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "A class prediction objective (sometimes called supervised classification) is a data transformation objective where the aim is to create a predictor from training data through a machine learning technique. The training data consist of pairs of objects (typically vectors of attributes) and
class labels for these objects. The resulting predictor can be used to attach class labels to any valid novel input object. Depending on usage, the prediction can be definite or probabilistic. A classification is learned from the training data and can then be tested on test data."@en 

- [class prediction objective](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200179) [label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "class prediction objective"@en 

- [class prediction objective](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200179) SubClassOf [data transformation objective](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200166)

### concretizes `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0000059`
#### Removed

- [concretizes](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0000059) [example of usage](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000112) "A journal article is an information artifact that inheres in some number of printed journals. For each copy of the printed journal there is some quality that carries the journal article, such as a pattern of ink. The quality (a specifically dependent continuant) concretizes the journal article (a generically dependent continuant), and both depend on that copy of the printed journal (an independent continuant)."@en 

- [concretizes](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0000059) [example of usage](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000112) "An investigator reads a protocol and forms a plan to carry out an assay. The plan is a realizable entity (a specifically dependent continuant) that concretizes the protocol (a generically dependent continuant), and both depend on the investigator (an independent continuant). The plan is then realized by the assay (a process)."@en 

- [concretizes](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0000059) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "A relationship between a specifically dependent continuant or process and a generically dependent continuant, in which the generically dependent continuant depends on some independent continuant in virtue of the fact that the specifically dependent continuant or process also depends on that same independent continuant. Multiple specifically dependent continuants or processes can concretize the same generically dependent continuant."@en 

- [concretizes](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0000059) [label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "concretizes"@en 

- [concretizes](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_0000059) Domain [process](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_0000015) or [characteristic](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_0000020)

### k-means clustering `http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200041`
#### Removed
- Class: [k-means clustering](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200041) 

- [k-means clustering](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200041) [definition](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/IAO_0000115) "A k-means clustering is a data transformation which achieves a class discovery or partitioning objective, which takes as input a collection of objects (represented as points in multidimensional space) and which partitions them into a specified number k of clusters. The algorithm attempts to find the centers of natural clusters in the data. The most common form of the algorithm starts by partitioning the input points into k initial sets, either at random or using some heuristic data. It then calculates the mean point, or centroid, of each set. It constructs a new partition by associating each point with the closest centroid. Then the centroids are recalculated for the new clusters, and the algorithm repeated by alternate applications of these two steps until convergence, which is obtained when the points no longer switch clusters (or alternatively centroids are no longer changed)."@en 

- [k-means clustering](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200041) [label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "k-means clustering"@en 

- [k-means clustering](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200041) SubClassOf [partitioning data transformation](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200171) 

- [k-means clustering](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200041) SubClassOf [class discovery data transformation](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200175) 

- [k-means clustering](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200041) SubClassOf ([has specified output](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0000299) some [clustered data set](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0000648)) and ([achieves_planned_objective](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0000417) some [class discovery objective](http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/OBI_0200178))
